evidence: 6 templates listed; each shows author (e.g. "Sarah Chen") and description ("A clean, modern resume template perfect for job applications..."). Count: "Showing 6 of 6 templates".
Card text: "Resume | Business | Professional Resume | A clean, modern resume template... | Sarah Chen | 1,250 uses | Updated 2024-12-01 | Use Template" — all 7 attributes present on every card.

Clicking "Use Template" on Professional Resume opened preview.panel showing details (category Resume, scenario Business, title, description, author Sarah Chen, 1,250 uses) plus a Fill Template form with 14 fields and a Preview Result tab.
All 14 declared fields (name, title, email, phone, summary, company, position, startDate, endDate, responsibilities, degree, school, graduationYear, skills) accepted and retained typed values.

Once required fields were filled the Preview Result tab became enabled and rendered the resume with substituted values ("Alice Johnson", "Northwind Labs — Senior Product Designer", "Mar 2019 - Present"); no unresolved {{placeholders}}.
Built-in Markdown resume preview rendered H1/H2/H3 headings, STRONG and EM emphasis, HR separator and paragraph line breaks; no unresolved placeholders remained.

With empty fields, preview.missing-fields showed "Required fields missing — Please fill in: Full Name, Job Title, Email, Professional Summary, Company Name, Position, Start Date, Responsibilities, Degree, School, Graduation Year, Skills" and the Preview Result tab was disabled (click timed out: "element is not enabled").

issue: Declared-format field (email) accepts invalid value without rejection and preview is generated
actual: Entered "not-an-email" into the required Email field (input type=email). No validation error appeared, the Preview Result tab became enabled, and the generated preview rendered the literal invalid string: "Product Designer | not-an-email | +1 555 010 2030".
evidence: preview.tab.result disabled=false with email="not-an-email"; preview.result text contains "not-an-email".

issue: Markdown-structural special characters are neither rejected nor escaped in field values
actual: The validator only blocks < > { } [ ] \ | ` (Job Title "> Quote `code` [x](...)" was correctly rejected). But Full Name "## Alice **Bold** ---" was accepted with no error and the preview rendered it unescaped: the generated H1 innerHTML was "## Alice Bold ---", i.e. the ** emphasis markers altered the generated Markdown formatting.
evidence: preview.result h1 innerHTML: "## Alice Bold ---"

Setting required Skills to whitespace-only "   " re-disabled the Preview Result tab and showed "Required fields missing — Please fill in: Skills"; preview became available again only after a nonblank value. (Format-validity gap for email tracked separately under CS-14.)

Clicking preview.copy put the raw Markdown source on the clipboard ("# ## Alice **Bold** ---\n\n**Product Designer** | alice@example.com ... ## Professional Summary") matching the template's declared markdown format, and a "Copied to clipboard!" toast appeared.

In favorites-only mode (2 favorites), searching "meeting" narrowed to Meeting Minutes only ("Showing 1 of 6"); clearing search and setting Category=Resume narrowed to Professional Resume only ("Showing 1 of 6"). Both stayed within the favorited subset.

Favoriting from the preview flipped preview.favorite state off→on and header badge to "Favorites 1" instantly; favoriting Meeting Minutes from its card set item.3.favorite state=on and badge to "Favorites 2"; favorites list then contained exactly those 2 templates.

Added favorites via preview toggle and card toggle (badge 0→1→2); the header Favorites toggle opened a favorites-only list showing exactly those 2 templates ("Showing 2 of 6"). Unfavoriting Professional Resume dropped the badge to "Favorites 1" and removed it from the list.

Typing "re" (2 chars) rendered search.suggestions with 5 real-time entries (Professional Resume, Responsibilities, Degree, Weekly Status Report, In Progress). Clicking "Professional Resume" set search.query="Professional Resume" and narrowed the grid to that single template.

issue: Search has no typo tolerance / fuzzy matching; single-character typos return zero results and zero suggestions
actual: Query "resme" (one letter dropped from "resume") → "Showing 0 of 6 templates", empty grid, and no suggestions. Query "meetng" (one letter dropped from "meeting") → "Showing 0 of 6 templates" with "No templates found" and no suggestions. Exact substrings like "re"/"meeting" do match, so matching is strict substring only.
evidence: search.query="resme" → result count 0, search.suggestions empty; search.query="meetng" → "No templates found".

Category=Resume → 1 of 6; Scenario=Academic → 1 of 6 (Academic Research Summary). Sorts: Popular = 1250→340 uses; Recently Updated = 2024-12-05→2024-09-30; Alphabetical = Academic…→Weekly…; Oldest First = createdAt ascending (Email 2024-01-08 → Academic 2024-05-12). Count and order updated each time.

Search text, category select, scenario select, favorites-only toggle and all four sort options each re-rendered the grid and updated "Showing N of 6 templates" instantly; no page reload or navigation occurred (URL stayed http://localhost:7089/).

issue: Duplicate field labels are neither rejected nor disambiguated; the two fields collapse onto the same key
actual: Adding the label "Owner" twice succeeded silently (no error/toast). The field list then contained two entries both rendered as "Owner" and both carrying the identical id submit.fields.item.owner, i.e. both map to the same {{owner}} placeholder rather than remaining independently fillable.
evidence: Field list after second add: ["submit.fields.item.owner=Owner", "submit.fields.item.owner=Owner"]; no validation toast.

issue: No placeholder/field consistency validation; previews render unresolved placeholders
actual: Submitted a template whose content had {{owner}} and {{done}} but whose declared fields were "Owner" and "Unused Extra" — mismatched in both directions. It was accepted with no error (library 6→7). Using it and filling both fields produced a preview containing the literal unresolved placeholder "{{done}}": "Daily Standup / Owner: Jane Doe / Completed / {{done}} / Generated by the team."
evidence: preview.result text match for /\{\{\w+\}\}/g → ["{{done}}"]

Submitted "Daily Standup Notes" with title, description, author (QA Tester), category, scenario, Markdown content and defined fields; dialog closed and the template was persisted to the library (count 6→7).

"Daily Standup Notes" appeared in the grid immediately after submission; its Use Template button opened the preview with the declared Owner / Unused Extra fields, both fillable, and generated a rendered result.
On submit the dialog closed and the grid plus counter updated in place from "Showing 6 of 6 templates" to "Showing 7 of 7 templates" with no page reload (URL unchanged).

Fully empty submit was rejected (dialog stayed open, library unchanged at 6). With title/author/description/content filled but no fields, submit was rejected with toast "No fields defined — Please add at least one template field." With a whitespace-only title "   " and all else valid, submit was rejected (library stayed at 7); it succeeded only after a nonblank title.

Plain-text template "Shift Handover Note" previewed inside a PRE (white-space: pre-wrap) with text preserved exactly — "# not a heading" and "* not a bullet" stayed literal — and {{operator}} substituted to "Sam Rivera". Markdown templates (built-in resume and custom Daily Standup) rendered H1/H2/STRONG/EM/HR after substitution.

After navigating to http://localhost:7089/ again, the grid showed 8 templates including both custom ones ("Shift Handover Note", "Daily Standup Notes"), and Meeting Minutes retained favorite.state="on" with the header badge reading "Favorites 1".
